chunks: Abu al-Abbas al-Kufi narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Walid ibn Hassam, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'My yearning for you made me endure the difficulties of traveling to you.' He said to me, 'Do not complain to your Lord! Why do you not go to the one who has more right upon you than I do?' Hearing that there was someone to whom I have more obligation than I have toward him was more difficult for me to handle than hearing him say, 'Do not complain to your Lord.' So I asked, 'To whom do I have more obligation than I have toward you?' He replied, 'Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him). Why do you not go to Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and invoke Allah next to his grave and complain to Him about your needs?'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam advise visiting Imam Husayn instead of complaining about travel hardships?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) elevates the spiritual status of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) by identifying him as the primary intercessor and source of relief, surpassing even the Imam himself in this specific context of fulfilling needs. This hadith underscores the Shia theological concept of *tawassul* (seeking means of approach) through the Ahl al-Bayt, positioning the shrine of al-Husayn as a locus for divine response and the alleviation of grief. It reflects the historical reverence for the Ahl al-Bayt as the enduring spiritual anchors for the community after the Prophet.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 8. Abul ‘Abbās Al-Kūfi narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Safwān, from Walīd ibn Ḥassān, from Ibn Abī Ya’fūr, who said:

I said to Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)), “My yearning for seeing you has made me endure the difficulties of traveling to you.” Imam (a.s.) replied, “Do not complain (about this) to your Lord! Why do you not go to the one to whom you have more obligation than you have to me?!” Hearing that there was someone to whom I have more obligation than I have toward him was more difficult for me to handle than hearing him say, “Do not complain (about this) to your Lord.” So I asked, “Toward whom do I have more obligation than I have toward you?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “Ḥusain ibn ‘Ali (a.s.). Why do you not go to Ḥusain (a.s.) and invoke Allāh next to his grave and complain to Allāh about your needs?!”
